```
$ git log --oneline -S '// Example: tl.fromTo' -- packages/cli/src/templates/blank/index.html
f059a6eb5 feat(cli): default BeginFrame, agent blank, and looks quality (#3927)
```

But the two templates are not in the same state, and `from-file` is the worse of the two:

```
$ git show f059a6eb5^:packages/cli/src/templates/from-file/index.html
fatal: path 'packages/cli/src/templates/from-file/index.html' exists on disk, but not in 'f059a6eb5^'
```

`from-file` did not exist before #3927. That commit created it, and created the timeline block already carrying `// Example: tl.from("#title", ...)` while `#title` existed only inside an HTML comment — so there has never been an element for it to animate. It has never passed `hyperframes check` on the audio-only path since the day it landed.

`blank` is different. It also shipped the example commented out, but it *does* render a real `#title`, so the fix is just uncommenting — which is what this PR does.

That asymmetry is why I did not just apply the same one-line change to `from-file`. Uncommenting its example builds a tween with zero targets, the sampled pixels do not change, and `sweep_static` fires anyway — I would be shipping a line that looks like a fix and is not. And `data-no-timeline` on the composition root would suppress the guard permanently for anyone who later adds their own overlay, which trades a loud false positive for a silent false negative.

For the record, `init --video` passes today only incidentally: the playing video changes the sampled pixels, so the fingerprint differs whether or not the timeline does anything. `init --audio track.m4a` has no such incidental cover and fails.

Two ways I can see this resolved, both maintainer calls rather than mine:

1. Give `from-file` a real overlay element to animate, so the template demonstrates the timeline contract the way `blank` does. Changes what a fresh A-roll project looks like.
2. Drop the GSAP timeline block from `from-file` entirely and treat it as the no-overlay scaffold it currently is. Then the open question is what the composition root needs for `sweep_static` to correctly stand down — the guard currently keys only off `data-no-timeline`, and there is no way to say "this composition has no timeline yet, but will" without permanently disarming the check.

Happy to take either as a follow-up PR once you have picked. I did not want to guess at which shape the template should have.
Held until the PR it stacks on merges; one open PR per lane. Reopens then.

Correction to my previous comment: **option 2 does not work.** I proposed "drop the GSAP timeline block from `from-file` entirely" as a viable resolution. It is not, and I should have checked before offering it.

`window.__timelines` registration is mandatory, not optional. Removing the timeline block from the `from-file` scaffold produces a hard lint error:

```
$ hyperframes init pristine --audio tone.m4a --non-interactive
$ # strip the trailing <script> that declares and registers the timeline
$ hyperframes check

[StaticGuard] Invalid HyperFrame contract: Missing `window.__timelines` registration.
Lint
  ✗ missing_timeline_registry: Missing `window.__timelines` registration.
  1 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info(s)
  ⚠ Browser session never ran — layout, motion, and contrast below are empty placeholders,
    not a clean pass.
  ◇ 0 issues across 0 sample(s)
◇  Check failed
```

The lint failure short-circuits the browser session, so the layout sweep never samples and the `0 issues` line is vacuous rather than green. There is also no `sweep_static` improvement to trade for it — the run fails either way, just earlier and with a less accurate message.

So `sweep_static` firing on `from-file` is not evidence that the template lacks a required registration. The template registers correctly; it registers an empty timeline. That was the wrong reading on my part.

This leaves one real option rather than two:

1. Give `from-file` a real overlay element and a live tween on it, so it has something to animate and demonstrates the timeline contract the way `blank` does. Changes what a fresh A-roll project looks like.
2. `data-no-timeline` on the composition root, which suppresses `sweep_static` but stays on the root permanently — so an author who later adds their own overlay and timeline has silently disarmed the check for their project.

I lean toward 1, because `from-file` is what `init` hands anyone who passes a media file, and a scaffold whose only lesson is "here is a commented-out example of something you cannot run" is the same defect as `blank` had. But it does change the template's starting appearance, so it stays your call. Say which and I will do it.

Unrelated, but worth crediting: that `⚠ Browser session never ran — layout, motion, and contrast below are empty placeholders, not a clean pass` line is exactly right. It caught my contaminated test run earlier and stopped me reporting a vacuous pass as a fix.

Thanks, Rames. At `1ea14145`:

**Fixed**
- **Skill authority (blocking 2):** `/hyperframes` § 6 now says any sender can claim to be the desktop app, so such a message is a request about this project only. It grants nothing beyond that, never approves anything, and never widens what the agent may do.
- **`app-tools.json` (non-blocking):** read only when it is an owner-only file of this user, with an `http` loopback URL on `/mcp/image/`. A copied project can no longer aim calls, or take answers, elsewhere. Tests cover a 0644 file and both kinds of foreign URL.
- **Desktop side (#2804, `71452005`):**
  - `agent-link.json` is followed only when it is owner-only and this user's.
  - A relay counts only as `http` on a loopback host at `/api/agent-link/message`.
  - A session is live only when its inbox is a socket this user owns.

**The relay (blocking 1): I'd like to keep it, and here is why.**

1. **The person is the sender, by their own choice.**
   - The hold protects a session that skips prompts from messages of *other* agents.
   - Through the relay, the only messages are ones the same person types in the desktop app, about the project they handed over themselves (Edit with Framey or `hyperframes open`).
   - They already chose no prompts for this session. The relay doesn't change what the session may do; it only lets their own words reach it from the other window.
   - Without it, every message they send from the app waits for a manual "let it in" in the terminal. That is the exact back-and-forth the app is there to remove.
2. **The hold is not a boundary against this user's own processes.**
   - Anything that can read the token as this user can also write `"crossSessionInbound": "accept"` to `~/.claude/settings.json`, which turns the hold off for the person's sessions altogether.
   - The same process could also add a hook, or edit the files the session is working on.
   - Reading the token adds no reach a same-user process lacks. Other users stay out (0600), as you noted.
3. **It is narrow.**
   - Loopback `Host` only and a timing-safe bearer.
   - It forwards only to the inbox of the session that started it, never to one from the file.
   - It exists only while that session keeps the preview as its own task, and ends with the session.
   - A stale relay is dropped as soon as the inbox changes.

If you still see a case where it reaches further than the session's owner can already reach, tell me which and I'll close it.

A related case from the same project, posted here rather than as a new issue because it is the same shape: an audit that silently skips content under a condition the author cannot see.

`contrast-audit.browser.js` probes text inside a `data-layout-allow-occlusion` element with `document.elementFromPoint` at a few points of its box and skips the element as intentionally occluded when something else answers. A sub-composition host is a full-frame box, so any host that comes later in the DOM and is visible at the sample time answers the probe for every allow-occlusion text block beneath it, even though the host paints nothing there. In the project this removed all eight contrast findings of a block the moment an unrelated small overlay scene was moved into a sub-composition with an overlapping time window. Neither `overflow` nor `pointer-events: none` on the sub-composition root changes it, because the host element itself takes the hit.

Two possible fixes from the outside: probe with `elementsFromPoint` and ignore hits that are composition hosts or roots with no painted background at that point, so only painted content counts as cover; or treat allow-occlusion as a declaration (skip only the layout occlusion finding) and still measure contrast against the pixels that are actually behind the text. A lint note that `data-layout-allow-occlusion` belongs on the covering element, not on the text that may be covered, would help too.

Worth stating the mechanism without reference to any tool, because GitHub documents all of it. From [Handling skipped but required checks](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks), three cases with three different outcomes:

| how the job skips | what the required check does |
|---|---|
| workflow bypassed by a path or branch filter | checks stay **Pending** and block merging |
| job skipped by its own `if:` conditional | **the job reports Success** |
| job skipped because a job it `needs` failed | the dependent is skipped and **may not block merging** |

The `!cancelled()` already in this job's condition is what decides which row applies, and it is the part that makes this a gate hole rather than a non-issue.

Without it, a failed `changes` would skip this job through the third row. With it, the conditional is evaluated instead: `needs.changes.outputs.edit_accuracy` on a failed job is the empty string, `== 'true'` is false, and the job skips **by its own `if:`**. That is the second row, where GitHub's documented behaviour is not "may not block" but reports Success. A required check reporting Success with nothing run.

So the failure needs no unusual conditions. `changes` runs `scripts/check-no-main-deletions.mjs`, a script whose purpose is to fail, and on the run where it fails the accuracy gate goes green.

The six sibling required checks already encode exactly this, each pairing `!cancelled()` or `always()` with a `needs.changes.result` test. This PR applies the same pairing to the one that is missing it. On the happy path the condition is unchanged.

One thing I should correct from the description above: it says the finding came from deadgate, and the detector that produced it has since been **removed from that tool**. I measured its output across 275 repositories and about 80% of what it reported was redundant with GitHub's needs-skip rule, the third row in the table, where the dependent skips anyway and the claim adds nothing. Deleting it was the right call on volume.

This repository is in the remainder, and `!cancelled()` is the reason. I am flagging that rather than leaving a citation to a tool that would no longer reproduce its own finding. The argument above does not depend on it either way: it is GitHub's documented behaviour, this job's existing condition, and the pattern already used by its six siblings.

**What changed since the first version**

Code-reviewed by GPT-6 Astra and human-reviewed with a short AWS Lambda test. The review found four problems; all are fixed:

1. **Redirects.** FFmpeg could follow a later redirect to plain HTTP or a private address. FFmpeg now reads from a small relay on `127.0.0.1`, which checks every redirect hop with the downloader's rules.
2. **Changed file, fallback path.** One fallback quietly read a replaced file. Every read now goes through the relay with `If-Match`, so it fails instead.
3. **Audio and duration probe.** These read the link without `If-Match`. Same fix.
4. **Blocking in the browser.** It ignored the query string, so it could block a different signed link to the same file. It now blocks the exact link (checked in headless Chrome).

One more thing came up while testing: Bun's `fetch` keeps downloading after FFmpeg hangs up, and Cloud Run runs on Bun. So the relay asks for the bytes in growing pieces (1 MB up to 8 MB), and a hang-up stops the transfer within one piece.

Lambda test of this exact commit: 1,000 frames of 4K from two 50-minute HEVC recordings on signed S3 links. Cost $0.119, a 1 MB plan with no video copied, and the same decoded picture and sound as the first version.

Thanks, both blockers were real. Fixed in `efcf1084`.

**Blocker 1: resolve cycle with `data-vfx-chain`.** Each of my wrappers now captures its own prior and returns at once when re-entered (`preparing`/`resolving` guards). A stale wrapper reached through core's `priorResolver` stops there, so the chain stays a constant depth. Neither side has to wrap the other into a growing chain. In the engine's order (vfx arms inside the seek, this hook after it returns) each owner runs exactly once per frame. In the reverse order, vfx's stale resolver also runs, which costs one extra capture and still terminates. `filmed-screen.test.mjs` copies `armPageComposite`'s shape verbatim and runs six frames in both orders. On `205d8318` it fails with the same `Maximum call stack size exceeded` you hit, and it passes now. I'd still take the core multi-owner registration point as the real fix; this guard is the component-side part.

**Blocker 2: second mount.** `mount()` now takes the snippet's own caller-scoped `document.querySelectorAll(".hf-filmed-screen")` and uses the first canvas without `data-filmed-screen-mounted`. Live check: the demo mounted twice through `data-composition-src` (0–4.5 s and 4.5–9 s) with a `fractal-noise` vfx-chain box on the same page. At `205d8318` the second instance is blank. Now both are filmed, each on its own clock, and the render finishes in 30 s with no console errors.

**Nits**
- **Unmount:** `mount()` returns `{ destroy() }`. It drops the lens, loses the GL context and removes the output canvas. A lens whose canvas leaves the page is pruned on the next frame. I left the seek hooks in place, because every lens on the page shares them.
- **Pending with zero lenses:** `arm()` returns early until a lens is mounted, so `__hf_page_composite_pending` is never set by an empty or fallen-back page.
- **No WebGL2:** steps aside the same way as no HTML-in-Canvas, with the scene back in the page and one warning.
- **Docs:** `fadeOut`, `zIndex`, `destroy()` and the canvas-list form are documented. The description no longer mentions cut tears, and `crt` is gone from the tags. The rack comment now says it measures where earlier targets sit in the DOM now.

**Also found while re-testing**
- A composition that isn't on screen yet, or any more, has no paint record. Its lens tried to capture every frame and logged "No cached paint record" (540 lines in the two-instance render). `draw()` now skips when the canvas fails `checkVisibility({ opacityProperty, visibilityProperty })`.
- `demo.html` pastes the library inline, and I had let it drift from the snippet. A test now fails if the two differ (whitespace aside).

Thanks Rames — all three points check out and are reworked in `be3f177`.

**Reproduced first.** `waitForNetworkIdle` defaults `concurrency: 0` in puppeteer-core 25.11 (`WaitForNetworkIdleOptions`, `@defaultValue 0`). Re-ran your table against `waitForPageReady` at head in headless Chrome (local server, `/hang` holds one request open, `/ping` beacon every 300 ms):

| page | as written | `concurrency: 2` |
|---|---|---|
| static | 519 ms | 503 ms |
| one long-poll fetch open | 15,003 ms | 502 ms |
| 300 ms beacon | 15,000 ms | 502 ms |

Matches your numbers almost exactly.

**What changed** (`be3f177`):

- `waitForPageReady(page, { timeoutMs, networkIdle })` now takes a single shared deadline — both call sites pass `min(15_000, remaining)` — split across the idle waits and the readyState poll. Each poll evaluate races the remaining deadline, so a hung execution-context wait stops at the deadline instead of ~30 s × 30 iterations.
- `waitForNetworkIdle` passes `concurrency: 2`.
- The poll rethrows `isDegradableEvaluateTimeoutError` instead of `.catch(() => true)` for everything — the stage degrades on protocol/stage timeouts like the rest of capture.
- `screenshotCapture.ts`: the click sweep returns how many elements it clicked, and `performance.timeOrigin` is compared around the sweep. The settle runs only when `clickedCount > 0` or the document changed (an unreadable pair reads as "can't prove unchanged" → settles on the safe side). A banner-free page pays the flat 400 ms as before.
- `coreExtractionPhase.ts`: the catalog-boundary call is `networkIdle: "after-load"` — it skips the leading idle wait, costs one readyState evaluate on a parsed document (~6–9 ms measured), and pays an idle wait only when the poll actually saw a loading document, all inside the same budget-capped deadline.

Same repro on the new head:

| page | `always` (post-click) | `after-load` (catalog) |
|---|---|---|
| static | 505 ms | 6 ms |
| one long-poll fetch open | 501 ms | 9 ms |

## 1. Requested test: `PRODUCER_ENABLE_BROWSER_POOL=false` fixes the Windows hang

The setup is the 15 s copy from the report (all 26 `<video>` and 165 `<audio>` kept, 11 with `data-color-grading`), with `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=450 HF_SEGMENT_BROWSER_RECYCLE=1 render --quality delivery --fps 30 --workers 3 --browser-gpu`, run on native Windows.

| `PRODUCER_ENABLE_BROWSER_POOL` | Browsers | Page loads | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unset (default) | 1 GPU Chrome | page 1 `page.goto complete (589ms)`; page 2 never completes | **fails**: `Navigation timeout of 180000 ms exceeded` (still reproduces on 0.8.154) |
| `false` | 3 GPU Chrome (one per worker) | each `page.goto complete` in about 0.6 s | **completes**: 450 frames, matches the non-segmented render (PSNR 51.5 dB, min 48.1) |

So the shared browser is the trigger.

One more observation with the pool off: the three worker sessions **initialise one after another**. Each `page.goto start` comes only after the previous session's `media + fonts + tailwind ready`, so any media-readiness wait is paid once per worker in series. In this trimmed copy, 24 out-of-range videos never become ready, so each session waits about 46 s. Capture took 3m18s, against 1m13s for `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=false` with 3 workers on 0.8.153, where the three `page.goto` calls start together.

## 2. New bug: segmented capture renders the first frame of a segment ungraded when a `data-color-grading` video is playing

**Found in a full render.** We rendered a 7:23 composition (13,303 frames, `HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=450`, WSL, BeginFrame) and compared it frame by frame with a non-segmented Windows render of the same composition. Three single frames, **5400, 6750 and 11250**, show the B-roll **ungraded** (brighter and cooler). The frames on either side are graded:

```
frame 6749: mean RGB 78 77 73
frame 6750: mean RGB 90 96 96   <- segment boundary
frame 6751: mean RGB 77 76 71
```

Those are exactly the 3 of the 29 segment boundaries that land inside a graded `<video>`. No other boundary shows a change, and the non-segmented render is clean at all three.

**Repro.** We used the same composition with `data-duration` set to 30 s. Graded `br01` (H.264 1920x1080 30 fps, muted, `class="clip"`) is on screen for frames 682 to 808, and `HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=700` puts a segment boundary inside it. Its grade is `{"preset":null,"intensity":1,"adjust":{"contrast":0.3,"highlights":-0.1,"blacks":-0.15,"temperature":0.35,"saturation":-0.35},"details":{"vignette":0.45,"vignetteFeather":0.65,"grain":0.5,"grainSize":0.3,"grainRoughness":0.6},"effects":{"tapeNoise":1,"tapeSpeed":0.5,...}}`, written by `hyperframes media-treatment --apply`.

Mean RGB at frames 698 to 702:

| Run | 698 | 699 | **700** | 701 | 702 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1: WSL, BeginFrame, segmented, `HF_SEGMENT_BROWSER_RECYCLE=1` | 72 50 43 | 71 50 44 | **91 66 62** | 71 50 44 | 71 50 45 |
| F2: WSL, BeginFrame, segmented, `HF_SEGMENT_BROWSER_RECYCLE=0` | 72 50 43 | 71 50 44 | **91 66 62** | 71 50 44 | 71 50 45 |
| F3: Windows, screenshot, segmented, `PRODUCER_ENABLE_BROWSER_POOL=false` | 70 48 42 | 70 48 42 | **90 64 61** | 70 49 43 | 69 49 44 |
| F4: Windows, screenshot, `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=false` | 70 48 42 | 70 48 42 | 70 48 42 | 70 49 43 | 69 49 44 |

All four runs used 3 workers and `--quality delivery --fps 30`. Both WSL runs logged `browserRecycles: 0`. Inside `br01` the only single-frame flash is frame 700, the only frame that jumps and then returns to its neighbours' colour. The other large frame-to-frame changes (684, 783, 808) are one-way: the clip's entry and its own motion.

So the flash is independent of platform, capture mode (BeginFrame or screenshot) and browser recycling. What it takes is **the first frame of a segment, landing in the middle of a graded video**. Our guess is that the first captured frame after a segment's seek is drawn before the grade pipeline has the video frame. We haven't tested whether a worker's first frame in a non-segmented render has the same problem when it lands inside a graded video. #4881 (`data-color-grading` readiness) might be related.

**Detection tip.** `check` and our cut checks don't catch this. A PSNR comparison against a non-segmented render does: it spikes at exact multiples of `HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES`.

Tested #5574 (`fix/wsl-gpu-full-chrome` at 600ffd0) on the NVIDIA machine: Windows 11, RTX 4070 SUPER, driver 616.92, WSL 2.4.13, Ubuntu 22.04, Mesa 23.2.1, user in `render`. Short version: **the fallback works, but only with Chrome 149 or older.** Every Chrome from **150** on fails the same way the headless shell does, and that includes `chrome@stable` (155 today).

## 1. As instructed: no GPU

`bun install` put Chrome for Testing **152.0.7977.42** in `~/.cache/puppeteer` (Puppeteer's postinstall). `resolveFullChromePath` takes the newest version there, so the render used it:

```
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → software (WebGL unavailable)
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → software (full Chrome: WebGL unavailable)
[hyperframes] WSL: the GPU check found no hardware GPU, so this render uses software WebGL (SwiftShader) and runs at CPU speed.
```

It rendered fine on SwiftShader: 450 frames, 2m15s.

## 2. With Chrome 139 as the newest full Chrome: works exactly as described

We moved 152 out of the cache, leaving 139.0.7258.154, and ran the same command:

```
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → software (WebGL unavailable)
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → hardware (full Chrome: WebGL renderer vendor="Google Inc. (Microsoft Corporation)" renderer="ANGLE (Microsoft Corporation, D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER), OpenGL ES 3.1)")
[BrowserManager] Browser launched (Chrome/139.0.7258.154, screenshot, gl=--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl, headlessShell=true, platform=linux)
```

It rendered 450 frames in **46.2s**, against 2m15s for run 1, and matches the SwiftShader output (PSNR 49.5 dB, min 46.9). GPU load peaked at 23%.

Caveat on that speed-up: this is our trimmed 15 s copy. Most of the gap is the headless shell's 45 s `media_readiness_timeout` per session on videos outside the trimmed duration, which full Chrome never hits. Measured after the pages are ready, all runs capture this light opening at about 23 to 31 frames/s. We haven't run a heavy composition in WSL on the GPU.

## 3. Bisect: Chrome 150 is where it breaks

We used `browsers install chrome@N` / `chrome-headless-shell@N` into a scratch path and probed WebGL with the CLI's Linux hardware flags (`--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl --enable-gpu-rasterization --ignore-gpu-blocklist --disable-software-rasterizer`):

| Build | WebGL renderer |
| --- | --- |
| full Chrome 139.0.7258.154 | D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER) |
| full Chrome 146.0.7680.165 | D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER) |
| full Chrome 149.0.7827.155 | D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER) |
| **chrome-headless-shell 149.0.7827.155** | **D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER)** |
| full Chrome 150.0.7871.124 | WebGL unavailable |
| full Chrome 151.0.7922.138 | WebGL unavailable |
| full Chrome 152.0.7977.42 | WebGL unavailable |
| full Chrome 155.0.8059.79 (`chrome@stable` today) | WebGL unavailable |
| chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30 (the CLI's) | WebGL unavailable |

From 150 on, the GPU process fails at initialisation (`CreateOffscreenGLSurface failed` → `Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization`). On 152 the log also shows the original report's `gl_surface_egl.cc: No suitable EGL configs found`. `--headless=new`, `--ozone-platform=x11|wayland`, `--use-angle=gl|vulkan` and `EGL_PLATFORM` overrides made no difference. Mesa's surfaceless display on D3D12 offers 48 pbuffer configs and 0 window configs (x11: 64 / 64), so something in 150 seems to have changed which configs it accepts.

**So the variable is the Chrome major, not headless shell vs full Chrome.** With **0.8.155 released** and `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` pointed at `chrome-headless-shell` 149:

```
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → hardware (WebGL renderer vendor="Google Inc. (Microsoft Corporation)" renderer="ANGLE (Microsoft Corporation, D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER), OpenGL ES 3.1)")
[BrowserManager] Browser launched (HeadlessChrome/149.0.7827.155, beginframe, gl=--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl, headlessShell=true, platform=linux)
beginframe capture · hardware gpu
```

That's **BeginFrame capture on the GPU in WSL**. The output matches (450 frames, PSNR 49.6 dB) and GPU load peaked at 73%.

## Suggestions

1. **Try every cached full Chrome, newest first, until one answers with hardware**, not only the newest. Each probe took under a second here. As it stands, the fallback picks a failing Chrome on any machine that has a recent one, and the note's `chrome@stable` installs one.
2. **Or cap Chrome at 149 under WSL with Mesa D3D12.** The existing `chromeMajorCeiling` mechanism could apply to the headless shell too, which keeps BeginFrame. In the note, `chrome@149` would be the install line that actually works today.
3. This looks like a Chromium regression in 150 for EGL on Mesa's D3D12 (WSLg) driver. We haven't filed it upstream. Happy to run a probe build if you have one.

Two minor notes:
- `bun run build` on Node 22.17.0 failed in `@hyperframes/sdk-playground` (`ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION ".ts"` for `packages/sdk/src/adapters/fs.ts`). It looks like it needs Node's type stripping (22.18 and later). `cli`, `engine` and `producer` built fine.
- Also on 0.8.155, the ungraded first frame of a segment is still there (previous comment). Thanks for queuing it.

Calibration data + gate-policy change pushed in `b1087b6f`.

## Real-fixture calibration

Method: drove the production regression fixtures through the same capture functions the verify path uses — compiled each fixture, rendered truth via `Page.captureScreenshot` (jpeg q=80), captured the same frame indices via the page-side `drawElementImage` API (`--enable-features=CanvasDrawElement`, Chromium 155), then ran the real `psnrDb`/`regionShift` on each pair. 56 pairs across 15 fixtures; `d3-adapter` timed out at 60s and is excluded.

| Fixture | Samples | PSNR (dB) | regionShift |
|---|---|---|---|
| fast-capture-gsap | 8 | 55.2–61.5 | 0 |
| parallel-capture-regression | 8 | 51.0–51.4 | 1 |
| gsap-letters-render-compat | 8 | 43.6–84.1 | 0–1 |
| animejs-adapter | 8 | 52.7–52.9 | 1 |
| gsap-call-render-seek | 4 | 50.7 | 1 |
| wysiwyg-subcomp-css | 4 | 49.7 | 1 |
| font-variant-numeric / variables-prod / css-import-scoping / many-cuts / sub-comp-t0 / nested-subcomp-depth-3 / missing-host-comp-id / subcomp-bare-fragment | 1–8 each | 49.2–inf | 0 |
| **css-spinner-render-compat** | 4 | 32.0–35.4 | **18–27** |

## The finding that decides the policy

`css-spinner-render-compat` is a `data-no-timeline` comp with a pure CSS `animation: spin` — DE-eligible, no gate routes it to screenshot. First suspicion was a DE rasterization defect, but the control runs show it is a truth-floor problem, not a DE problem:

- two back-to-back **screenshots** of the same seek: PSNR 34.3 dB, shift 23
- a second **screenshot-vs-screenshot** pair at the same frame: PSNR 34.8 dB, shift 22
- same comparison after 5s idle: inf / 0

The CSS animation phase is nondeterministic under the capture sequence, so even truth-vs-truth disagrees far above the proposed ceiling. Combined with your synthetic results (gamma 1.04 → 4, +1px stroke → 10) and the #3345 repro needing ≥3–5, **no default threshold separates the damage class from this benign class** — default-on would cost screenshot fallbacks on legitimate renders.

## What changed

- `HF_DE_VERIFY_MAX_SHIFT` is now unset-by-default observe-only: the shift is still computed and logged on every verified sample, and the observed max feeds a new `verifyMaxShiftObserved` drain stat → `drawElement.verifyMaxShiftObserved` on the perf summary → `de_verify_max_shift_observed` on `render_complete` telemetry. Setting it in [1, 64] arms the fail-closed gate exactly as before (both streaming and parallel-disk paths, same `kind: "shift"` error → screenshot fallback).
- Your telemetry ask landed in `8784b51d`: `failedShift`/`verifyMaxShift` propagate through `deVerifyFallbackTelemetry` → `de_fallback_failed_shift` + `de_fallback_max_shift` on `render_error`, plus the crash-survival observability mirror.
- This gives us the clean-render production distribution needed to pick a real ceiling — or to scope the gate to non-nondeterministic comp classes (e.g. skip when the comp has wall-clock CSS animation) before arming it.

Recommendation: keep it observe-only until telemetry shows where production clusters land; the env escape hatch arms it immediately for any install that wants fail-closed now.

I'd like to take this one. The review on the closed #4059 asked for the real errno from Windows hardware, so I measured that first. It changes the shape of the fix.

## What Windows actually returns

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 x64, Node v24.20.0, ffmpeg 9.0.2 (gyan.dev). I spawned a copy of `ffmpeg.exe` while a second process held it open with different .NET `FileAccess`/`FileShare` modes. Defender real-time protection was off, so this **simulates** the lock instead of catching an AV scan in the act:

| Holder of the exe | `spawn()` result | After the holder closes |
|---|---|---|
| read, `FileShare.None` | **sync throw** `EBUSY` (-4082), syscall `spawn` | ok |
| write, `FileShare.Read` | **sync throw** `EBUSY` | ok |
| write, `FileShare.ReadWrite` | **sync throw** `EBUSY` | ok |
| read, `FileShare.Read` | ok | ok |
| ACL denies execute (permanent) | **sync throw** `EPERM` (-4048) | ok after the ACL is restored |
| missing exe | `'error'` event `ENOENT` | n/a |

Rewriting the exe and spawning it right away 30 times, and spawning it 64 times at once without a lock, never failed. So the "sibling invocation" theory doesn't reproduce, but any handle with write access or no sharing does.

Two consequences:

1. **`EBUSY` is the right errno, and `EPERM` should stay out**: here `EPERM` is the permanent ACL case.
2. **`EBUSY` is thrown synchronously from `spawn()`.** Node only delivers `EACCES`, `EAGAIN`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE` and `ENOENT` through the `'error'` event. Everything else throws before a `ChildProcess` exists ([`ChildProcess.prototype.spawn`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.x/lib/internal/child_process.js)). So `ManagedChildProcess.onError` / `reason: "spawn_error"` never sees it. A retry keyed on the `spawn_error` outcome (the approach in #4059) would not fire for this bug on `runFfmpeg`, `ffprobe.ts` or `audioPadTrim`.

## What each managed-binary call site does today

There are 10 call sites that start `getFfmpegBinary()`/`getFfprobeBinary()` outside tests. With a sync `EBUSY`:

- Fails the operation with a bare `spawn EBUSY`: `runFfmpeg.ts` (`spawnFfmpeg`), `ffprobe.ts` (`runFfprobe`), `streamingEncoder.ts`, `audioExtractor.ts` (inside the `new Promise` executor), `audioPadTrim.ts` (`runFfprobeJson`), `gpuEncoder.ts` (`detectGpuEncoder`), `psnr.ts`, `distributed/shared.ts` (`readFfmpegVersion`).
- Silently degrades for the life of the process: `gpuEncoder.ts` `canUseGpuEncoder` → `.catch(() => null)` caches "no usable GPU encoder", and `psnrFilterAvailability.ts` caches `null` ("no filters") after its catch-all.

## Proposed fix

- One engine helper that retries **only the synchronous `spawn()` throw** with code `EBUSY` or `ETXTBSY` (the POSIX equivalent). Nothing has started at that point, so the retry has no side effects. I'm proposing 3 attempts with 250 ms / 500 ms backoff, each retry logged with the binary path. The `execFile`-based sites (`psnr`, `psnrFilterAvailability`, `readFfmpegVersion`) retry the same rejection.
- When the retries run out, the error keeps `.code` and names the binary path and errno, with the hint "another process held the executable open (often antivirus scanning it)".
- Adopted at all 10 sites, so the two caches above can no longer store a result produced by a transient lock.
- Tests: unit tests for the classification and backoff (a fake `spawn` that throws `EBUSY` n times, plus `EPERM`/`ENOENT` passing straight through), and a per-site test that the retry is wired in. I'll also attach the Windows repro script to the PR.

Open question for @miguel-heygen / @miga-heygen: is 3 attempts / ~750 ms total acceptable, or would you rather allow a longer window (for example 5 attempts, ~4 s) since a full AV scan of a 100+ MB `ffmpeg.exe` can take longer?

Follow-up on the colour note, at `541f8a77`: measured, confirmed, fixed.

**Measurement.** One HLG render holds three copies of the same red/green bars, sampled as raw BT.2020 code values (16-bit):

1. an SDR BT.709 clip;
2. the HLG version of the same bars with a no-op `filter: saturate(1)`, so it takes the tone-map path;
3. the HLG version unfiltered.

| red patch | SDR clip | tone-mapped clip | native HLG |
|---|---|---|---|
| previous head | 60449 28472 11173 | **61201 10149 0** | 45961 21093 11426 |
| this head | 60449 28472 11173 | 51699 26915 16205 | 45961 21093 11426 |

The tone-mapped clip carried BT.709 values unconverted into the BT.2020 output, so it was visibly oversaturated next to its SDR neighbour. Green showed the same.

**Fix.** In an HDR render, the tone-map pass now takes the same BT.709 to BT.2020 step the SDR clips get, applied after the tone-map:

- `toneMapVideosToSdr` passes the render's transfer;
- the extractor records it through `sdrToHdrTransfers`, the one array both the cache key and the extraction read, so these frames get their own cache entry.

The two filters swap order (tone-map, then remap); they never combined before. Forced-SDR renders are unchanged.

**Test.** `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` "gives a tone-mapped clip in an HDR render the BT.2020 primaries of its SDR neighbours" extracts the same colour as SDR and as HLG together for an HLG render.

- With the fix, the tone-mapped frame's saturation is within 0.03 of the SDR clip's (0.366 vs 0.368).
- On the previous head the gap is 0.08.

**Timed overlay without an id dropped from HDR exports** (found by another contributor, item 137).

The rule: any timeline-registry read the analyzer can't resolve to exact keys (anything dynamic or registry-wide, such as `Object.keys(window.__timelines)` or `__timelines[id]`) keeps every scene eager for that reader; a string key or a dot key (`__timelines.b`, `?.b`, `["b"]`) counts as resolved.

The registry's own setup (`= window.__timelines || {}`, `??=`, `||=`, `= {}`, `if (!window.__timelines)`, `typeof`) reads nothing, and neither does a computed-key write. A named key names that scene. **Blocker, forward with no deadline:** `forward()` now passes `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)` (`FORWARD_DEADLINE_MS`). The abort lands in `withHistory`'s `.catch(() => null)`, so a stopped or wedged owner gives #5821's 409 with the reason within 5 s, the same bound as the owner wait. New test: `answer the 409 with the reason when the owner takes the request and never replies`. The owner advertises a `127.0.0.1` server that accepts and never answers, and the claim must come back 409 in under 9 s. With the `signal` line removed it times out at 15 s; with it, 31 passed, 3 runs in a row.

One consequence, also listed in the body: a forwarded undo that takes longer than 5 s (large media) answers 409 while the owner finishes it. The owner's log stays correct.

**Nit, 404 to 409:** left as is. A 404 from the owner can be its real answer (`/blob/<hash>` for a file it does not keep), so mapping every forwarded 404 to the 409 would hide correct replies. The port-reuse case also needs the owner pid to be alive and still in `owner.pid` while another server holds its port, which only happens if the owner closed its server but kept running and kept the lock. Happy to add it if you see that case in practice.

**[P2] Preserve foreground capacity while background encoders are stopped.** Agreed: the stopped child kept its counted slot until `transcodeToCache`'s `finally`. Now each job records whether it holds a slot:

- Stopping a background copy frees its slot at once (`stopCopy` → `releaseSlot(job)`), so the next queued copy, including a compatibility copy, starts during the hold.
- A stopped copy resumes only into a free slot (`resumeCopy` checks `activeTranscodes < MAX_CONCURRENT_TRANSCODES` before `SIGCONT`). If none is free, it stays stopped and the existing one-second hold timer retries. Resumed encoders never take the count past the cap.
- `releaseSlot(job)` is a no-op for a job that holds none, so a copy killed while stopped (timeout, replacement) does not release twice.
- The same stall also hit a request for the stopped copy itself: a non-background ask joined the background job and waited while it stayed stopped. A non-background ask now clears `background` on the job it joins and resumes it. Both join paths go through one `raise()`. The covered-box path never prioritized before; it now does too.

Tests (`proxyTranscoder.test.ts`; file exit 0, 58 passed, 3 runs in a row):
- Your scenario at saturation: two background copies fill both slots, playback stops both, a foreground copy then spawns at once (3 encoders started). On pause exactly one stopped copy resumes; the second resumes after the foreground copy finishes and frees a slot.
- A viewer asking for a stopped background copy resumes it while playing.
- A priority ask served by a larger queued copy moves that copy ahead of an earlier normal one.
- Mutations, each restored: not freeing the slot on stop fails 5 tests; resuming without a free slot fails exactly the saturation test; leaving a viewer's ask background fails exactly the viewer test; skipping `raise` on the covered path fails the viewer and priority tests.

Thanks, both blockers reproduced and are fixed in `b513296a7`.

**Blocker 1 (a failing helper fails the check).** Reproduced with real Chrome: `kill -9` of the second Chrome during a `heygen-promo-preview-assets` check lost the whole browser pass on 3/3 runs (`check_runtime_failure: Attempted to use detached Frame`, browser checks skipped). Fix in `collectGridSamples`: each helper runs inside its own `try`. On failure, every sample it took (finished or in flight) goes back on the queue, its `perTime` slots are cleared, and it marks its log `"drop"`. After draining, the first page waits for the helpers still mid-sample, then redoes anything handed back. The merge is now a stable sort by time, so redone samples land where one page would have logged them. Nothing is left without a handler, so there is no `unhandledRejection`. The same kill now gives findings identical to one Chrome on 3/3 runs, with no Chrome left running.
Tests: your scenario (helper throws on its second seek) equals the serial result with no unhandled rejection. A browser-level case where the second Chrome crashes mid-grid and logs a crash message reports exactly the one-Chrome messages. Removing the catch, the requeue, the slot clearing or the log drop each fails a test.

**Blocker 2 (memory gate ignores cgroup limits).** `free` is now `Math.min(os.freemem(), process.availableMemory())`. Unit case: 100 GB host free with 400 MB available keeps one Chrome (fails with `os.freemem()` alone).

**Nits**
- Short grids paying for a second Chrome start: fixed. The first page no longer waits for a helper that is still opening. Once the grid is done, the helper's open is cancelled (an AbortSignal for the launch phase, plus closing its Chrome for navigation and settle; the close is the shared memoized `closeManagedBrowser`, so cleanup still awaits it and reports its error). `--at 1,2` on fast-capture-gsap: a 4-core box now matches a box with one Chrome (median 1.57 s vs 1.68 s). Test: a second Chrome that never finishes opening is cancelled, and the check reports what one Chrome reports (it hangs without the cancel).
- Primary failure waiting on `helperOpen`: the `finally` now cancels the helper the same way before awaiting it, so the error surfaces without waiting for navigation or render-ready timeouts.
- Opt-out switch: not adding one. With the fallback, a helper that misbehaves costs speed and never findings, and this change adds no new flags or env knobs. Happy to revisit if a setup turns up where the second Chrome is slower.
- `contrastMs`: commented where it is summed (it sums both pages, so with two Chromes it can exceed wall time); also noted in the PR body.

**Red check (Tests on windows-latest: engine-cli):** `frameCapture-videoMetadataHints.browser.test.ts` timed out in `afterAll` (`browser.close()` past the 10 s hook limit). This PR touches only `packages/cli`, and that workflow failed once in its last 40 runs. The root fix is in #5898: a bounded close for the engine's browser-test fixtures (close, then SIGKILL and disconnect, matching `closeBrowserAfterFailedProbe`).

Verification: CLI unit suite 4845 passed; `check.test.ts` and `checkBrowser.test.ts` 3 runs green; tsc, oxlint, oxfmt and fallow clean; findings identical between one and two Chromes on all 3 fixtures (6/6) at this head.

@vanceingalls fixed at 27f1b2e8 (head f6dfd37e only shortens a doc comment):

1. **Blocker, missing summary:** fixed. The parser now uses `?? "nan"`, so a run with no `Peak:` line throws "FFmpeg did not report AAC true peak" again, on both the whole-file and segmented paths. The new test `audioTruePeak.fakeFfmpeg.test.ts › throws when ffmpeg prints no true-peak summary` feeds frame lines with no summary. With `?? ""` put back it fails with `promise resolved "+0" instead of rejecting`.
2. **Nit, sibling scans keep running:** fixed. A local controller is merged with the caller's signal through `AbortSignal.any` and aborted when `Promise.all` rejects (same pattern as `parallelCoordinator.ts`). The test `stops the other segment scans when one fails` fails without the abort (`[false, false]`).
3. **Nit, non-48 kHz rates:** fixed. Only `sampleRate === 48_000` is split into segments; any other rate gets one whole-file pass. The test `measures a rate other than 48 kHz in one whole-file pass` fails without the fix (3 ffmpeg runs instead of 1).

Checked on Linux: producer typecheck clean; `audioTruePeak.test.ts` (real ffmpeg) plus the new file pass 7/7, three runs in a row; `audioPadTrim.test.ts` 38/38; oxfmt, oxlint and fallow clean.

Thanks so much for the careful review, @vanceingalls! I took all four suggestions:

- **الله stays whole**: the split examples now keep the word as one piece, since splitting it breaks the ligature in fonts like Cairo and Alexandria.

- **Hebrew note**: the typography reference now says Open Sans covers Hebrew.

@terencecho thanks, fixed in 216b0221 (rebased on main):

- **[P2] missing identity authorizing deletion:** `inThisPidScope` now requires a known scope: a boot identity, and on Linux the pid namespace too. Otherwise the owner is "unknown" and the dir is kept. Stamping without uptime is unchanged; known matching or mismatching scopes, live pids and staging backups behave as before.

- **Regression you asked for:** boot and pid namespace both unavailable, a matching `work-<uuid>-` owner record with a pid that does not exist here: the dir is retained and the new work dir is still created. It fails on 6d8f8c65.

- **Coverage:** the new cases go through `createRenderWorkDir`, the same sweep the orchestrator calls. Each passed 3 runs in a row; `renderDirOwner.test.ts` (2) and `artifactTransaction.test.ts` (25) pass.

Thanks. On the open contract (unrelated commands start with `esbuild`, `puppeteer-core` and `sharp` absent), here is the runtime evidence rather than source reading:

1. **Executed with the packages deleted.** The "Why" table runs the packed CLI with all three deleted from the install: `--version`, `init`, `info`, `compositions` and `lint` exit 0 at this head; on main, `init`, `info`, `compositions` fail with `Cannot find package`. `validate` and `compare` still need esbuild to bundle, by design, and say so.

A static import in an unread helper such as `browserLeasePool.ts` would land in a chunk and fail that check.
3. **Legacy runtime-file readers:** every reader of the removed `dist/hyperframe-runtime.js` was changed or already accepted `hyperframe.runtime.iife.js`; the packed-tarball run above loads the runtime through those readers.

If a specific reader or command is still in doubt, name it and I'll run it with the packages deleted.

Thanks, all three points are addressed at `c3ba2bd4` (security changes in `d16e48f2`).

**Blocker: impersonation and env disclosure.** Both of your fixes, together.
- The endpoint lives in a per-user private directory: `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyperframes-warm`, else `~/.cache/hyperframes/warm` (`LOCALAPPDATA\hyperframes\warm` on Windows). After `mkdir 0700`, the directory is `lstat`ed and must be a real directory (not a symlink), owned by `getuid()`, with no group or other bits. Anything else means the check runs cold.
- That directory holds a random 32-byte token in a `0600` file, created with `wx` and checked the same way.
- The Windows pipe name is an HMAC of that token, so it can't be predicted or squatted.
- Mutual handshake before any request. The client sends only a nonce. The server must answer with `HMAC(token, nonce)` and its own nonce, or the client hangs up and runs cold; a server that stays silent is given up on after 2 s. The client then proves the token over the server's nonce.
- The request no longer carries the environment. It sends an HMAC digest of it, which the warm process compares with its own.
- A request with a wrong proof is declined, and the process keeps waiting for a genuine client.
- Tests:
  - a 0777 directory, a symlinked directory, a 0644 token and a symlinked token each fall back to cold;
  - an impostor holding the socket with a forged proof, and a silent impostor, each receive only the client's nonce, and the check runs cold;
  - a request with a wrong proof is declined, then a genuine client is served.
- Mutation checks: these tests fail when the client trusts any server, when the directory checks are removed, when the server trusts any client, or when the handshake timeout is removed.

**Socket file mode.** Covered by the verified 0700 directory, as you suggested.

**Unbounded frame length.** `frameReader` now refuses frames over 64 MB, and both sides drop the connection. There is a test, and removing the cap makes it fail.

Separately, `c3ba2bd4` fixes a bug the new tests surfaced: the client stopped writing frames after the first one, so a check that printed a notice to stderr lost its JSON report. That fix has a regression test.

**Clip lane gain now follows the transport.** The clip's FX handle books the lane gain as one more target (`attachClipStages` in `webAudioTransport.ts`, `scheduleVolume` in `audioFx.ts`), so it rides the paths that already re-aim the FX lanes:

**1. Backspace and Reset Keyframes.** The frame no longer arms a Delete combo that equals the Reset Keyframes binding while reset may claim it. "May claim" means the selected clip has keyframes, which is the condition the dispatcher checks before calling reset. That condition now has one owner, `resetKeyframesMayClaim` in `appHotkeysDispatch.ts`, used by both the dispatcher and the arm. In that case Backspace is forwarded to Studio, whose dispatcher tries reset first and falls through to clip Delete as before. Delete itself still runs in-frame.
Test: "leaves Backspace with Studio while Reset Keyframes may claim it for the selected clip". Without the carve-out it fails: Backspace removes the clip in-frame.

**2. Cold first nudge on a GSAP clip.** Each nudge step now carries `baseGsap`: the GSAP x/y of every GSAP-owned handle, read before the burst's first draw. The frame already held these bases for its own draw. When Studio starts a session from a runtime step, either from the read-ahead or from a fresh gesture-start read, GSAP members start from that pre-draw x/y instead of the drawn one. The event parser at the port checks the new field.
Test: "starts a cold first nudge on a GSAP clip from its pre-draw position, so the step lands once". It forces the read-ahead cold, presses ArrowRight once on a clip at GSAP x 40, and checks that the commit's stamped GSAP base is 40 and the clip ends at 41. Without the fix the stamped base is 41. ## What

Frame extraction no longer lets every ffmpeg it runs at once start one thread per core. When extraction runs overlap, each one gets its share of the CPU budget (`-threads` for decode and encode, `-filter_threads`); an extraction running alone keeps ffmpeg's own defaults, exactly as on main.

## Why

Extraction runs up to `usableCpuCount() / 2` ffmpeg processes at once (`EXTRACTION_SLOTS`). Left to its default, each of them also starts threads per core, and each thread holds frames, so memory grew with cores x slots x frame size. One 4K 60 fps mjpeg source extracted to 1080p JPEGs peaked at 211 MB with `-threads 2` and 1057 MB with `-threads 32`, at the same wall time. A Windows export with three 4K sources failed in extraction with ffmpeg "Cannot allocate memory" on a machine with 32 GB+ of RAM.

A first version gave every run a fixed `cpuBudget / EXTRACTION_SLOTS` share; it made a lone extraction up to 76% slower (one H.264 1080p clip on 8 cores: 1585 ms on main, 2796 ms), so the share now depends on how many runs actually overlap.

## Related work

None.

## How

- One count of extraction runs planned or running, owned in `videoFrameExtractor.ts`: `extractVideoFramesRange` adds 1 before its first await and a segmented extraction adds its extra workers before starting them; each removes its share in a `finally` (success, failure, abort). Every fan-out calls `extractVideoFramesRange` without awaiting first, so siblings are counted before any of them can take a free slot.
- When a run's slot is granted: alone (count 1) it passes no thread flags, so its argv is main's; otherwise it gets `floor(cpuBudget / min(EXTRACTION_SLOTS, count)) + 1` threads as `-filter_threads`, `-threads` before the input and `-threads` on the output. The `EXTRACTION_SLOTS` limit is unchanged.

Two additions to the description, as of `e7149ed4`:

- **A film's own observers see the host.** During a sealed drag, the host is a child of `<html>`, so a film's own `MutationObserver` on the document gets one add when the drag starts and one remove at release. Per-step placement writes stay inside the closed shadow root and never reach it. An open preview adds nothing. The host is removed at release, on cancel, when the last draft ends, and when the agent is disposed.
- **CSS escapes are refused.** `style.setProperty` decodes CSS escapes, so `u\72l(...)` or `\75rl(...)` would become a `url()` and make the frame fetch. A chrome value may not contain a backslash; computed paint values never need one. `dragChrome.test.ts` "refuses a copy over the node or byte caps, and anything but paint" now covers both escape forms. It fails without the check (`expected true to be false`) and passed 3 runs in a row.

Update at `6e647286`, from an adversarial pass over the whole sealed path (late answers, retries, stalls, deadlines, re-primes):

- **Retry preview keeps the token that was working.** Retry now asks for the current token starting from the address it last loaded (`underCurrentFrameToken`), so a failed or stalled lookup keeps that address instead of dropping to the bare preview path. Retry no longer takes a primed token either: one primed while the preview is open waits for the next preview of that project.
- **A refused preview page carries the runtime.** `previewRefusalPage`, which every page served to a refused frame goes through (the too-large and refused sub-composition pages, and the 4xx/5xx pages from `answerRefusedFrameWithPage`), now includes the runtime after the refusal it reports. A sealed frame then reports the refusal through the runtime as it did when the player added the runtime itself, and `src-carries-runtime` holds for every page the server answers a project preview frame with. In an open frame the refusal is still read straight from the page as before. `withPreviewRuntime` and the refusal page share one tag builder, `previewRuntimeTag`.

Thanks. Agreed on the note, and it stays out of this PR. A resize that starts without a press (the size fields, the agent resize tool) reads the box from the element's last press. If that element hasn't been pressed since, it gets nothing and records `0` / `0`, as main does. It gets an out-of-date box only when the element's size changed after that press and before its first Studio resize; the stamp is written once, on that first resize. The fix is to ask the frame for the element's live layout when no press measured it, so it goes in a follow-up PR with its own test.
